verification.note: file_question.py:1038-1051: close() moves the document into a local, and when PYMUPDF_LOCK.acquire(timeout=max(0, end-now)) fails it returns. The comment says 'its holder or the garbage collector closes the document', but nothing hands the document to the lock holder, so the local's refcount drop finalizes it unlocked in the to_thread worker. The case is reachable: rag.py:2285-2298 catches PageImageUnavailable from source.page_count() or image() after open() succeeded, and rag.py:2352 then calls close() with the budget spent. Also at file_question.py:1027-1036, `return pixmap.tobytes(...)` inside `with self._locked()` releases the lock before the frame drops `page` and `pixmap`, so their finalizers run unlocked on every render. I8 says every PyMuPDF call that renders runs under the lock, and pdf.py:60-63 says every PyMuPDF call in the addon holds it. Whether a finalizer drop racing an extraction actually corrupts MuPDF state was not run.

file_question.py:987-995: an absolute stored path is returned as is, and a relative one goes through config.resolve_stored_path(config.resolve_file_path(...)) (config.py:1283-1304), which uses more of config.py than settings.drive_mounts. config.py:1297-1299 says the stored IndexedFile.file_path is already the on-disk spelling, so skipping normalisation for absolute paths matches how paths are stored. This is a touch-point scope point, not a behavior defect.

rag.py:2864-2875: `first = False` after any delta, and later waits use timeout=None, so no keep-alive `None` is yielded again. rag.py:1746-1758 (inside _document_tool_answer, which starts at rag.py:1593) holds leading whitespace deltas with `continue` and writes no answer_chunk. After a whitespace-only first delta the stream writes nothing until visible text arrives. The hold appears only in the document path (no other `held =` in rag.py). The gap lasts only as long as the model pauses after leading whitespace, which is usually short.

file_question.py:934-949: the title comes from row.position['title'], is cut with title[:60], and is written as `{label}: {title} — {excerpt}`. Only the excerpt goes through _without_markers and whitespace collapse (file_question.py:973-984). So a stored title containing `[1]` or a line break reaches a contents line unchanged. Spec item 3 (docs/specs/file-ask-document-tools.md:93-99) asks only for the title cut to 60 characters, with marker removal stated for the excerpt alone, so the code follows the spec's letter. A title carrying a bracketed number would still put one on a line that names a section, against I5.

unspecified_scores.reason: Only when a page request's lock wait times out while an extraction holds the lock does the PDF get finalized outside the lock; the user would at most see a rare failed extraction or a wrong render.
Stored absolute paths are already the on-disk spelling (config.py:1297-1299), so no ordinary condition gives the user a different result.
A model that starts its final answer with whitespace and then pauses leaves the stream silent; the user sees a brief stall, or a proxy timeout only if the pause is long.
For a PDF whose indexed rows carry no page, the contents show bare page ranges and get_text by page says nothing is written, so the model cannot read further text and the user gets a weaker answer.
An EPUB whose section title holds a bracketed number or a line break puts it into the contents, which can mislead the model's citations or break a line; the user sees an odd citation at worst.
A cut PDF without a pdf_markdown row or page units gets a get_text definition reading 'from 1 to 0' and no page count, so page-based reading fails and the answer rests on passages alone.

specification_compliance: The document contents line format follows spec item 3, which cuts the title to 60 characters and removes markers only from the excerpt; this leaves a gap against I5 for titles that carry bracketed numbers.
PageImages takes PYMUPDF_LOCK for open, page_count and image, but Python finalizers of the Document, Page and Pixmap can run after the lock is released, which bears on I8.

potential_unspecified_behavior.behavior: A contents group whose rows all reduce to empty text after marker removal is written as the range alone, the same as a group with no row.
potential_unspecified_behavior.reason: Rare rows made only of markers or whitespace make the contents show a bare range; the model sees no excerpt for that group.

regression_risks: A finalizer of a pymupdf Document, Page or Pixmap running unlocked at the same time as a long extraction could, in principle, disturb MuPDF state shared with the extraction.
test_coverage: The document-tool scenario is in SCENARIOS, so it is covered by the file-block and S179/S181 placement tests, and it is left out of the I7 byte-for-byte check through TODAYS_PATHS.
I found no test of close() giving up on the lock or of an EPUB title that contains markers.
not_verified: I did not run any test or exercise PyMuPDF finalizers concurrently, so whether an unlocked drop actually corrupts an extraction is unconfirmed.
I did not inspect the git diff itself to confirm the golden file is new in this commit.
I did not check whether the final-request keep-alive gap can exceed a real proxy timeout.
